title: Number of Integers With Popcount-Depth Equal to K I
summary: Given the integers n and k , find the count of integers in the range [1, n] whose popcount-depth is exactly k .
statement: Given the integers n and k , find the count of integers in the range [1, n] whose popcount-depth is exactly k . The popcount-depth of an integer x is defined as the smallest integer d ≥ 0 such that applying the popcount function d times results in 1. The popcount function counts the number of 1's in the binary representation of x .
constraints: One <= n <= 10^15 and zero <= k <= five.
Depth is the minimum repeated-popcount applications needed to reach one.
Count integers from one through n with depth exactly k.
hints: For x>1, its depth is one plus the depth of popcount(x), which is at most the bit length.
Group integers by number of set bits and count each group up to n combinatorially.
Scan n from high bits to low, adding binomial choices whenever a one bit may be replaced by zero.
Every integer is counted by its unique first lower bit choice, and the small set-bit count determines its remaining depth.
editorial: Every integer is counted by its unique first lower bit choice, and the small set-bit count determines its remaining depth.

tests.explanation: Powers two and four have one set bit and depth one.
Three, five, and six have two set bits and depth two.
